# Council: Sherlock general-purpose recursion design decisions (run `sherlock-gp-decisions-council-20261110`)

Date: 2026-11-10. Owner request: "Have a group of agents pick all of these". Advisory under the council protocol (`~/.claude/skills/council/`). The owner keeps the final call.

## The decisions (answer every one)

- **D1 Genesis mechanism.** How is the canonical initial state of a run enforced? Options: (a) an in-circuit check on the first leaf (gated on `h_pre == 0`) that the pre carriers are the canonical initial state for `prog_d`, including fuel and stack limit; (b) off-chain recomputation of `init_d` by the independent verifier and readers, with `acceptRun` restated as a claim relative to the sealed `init_d`; (c) another authenticated mechanism you propose. E3 measures the cost of (a) and is still running. Measured so far: genesis carriers differ in length per program (prefix 290 lanes for `literal`, 271 for `add`), so carriers are not padded to `Bounds`.
- **D2 Leaf architecture, given the measured leaf size.** Measured on 2026-11-10 by `cost_model` (qualification config `testdata/dispatch/config.json`, fact(3) first step; branch `worktree-agent-acf90d07b6b60767c`, commits `5782173bd`, `7fadf00c3`):
  - per side 1,726 lanes (image 256, data 1,383, helper 87); shared prefix 403;
  - single-rule circuits: `KMachineEvalBinary` k=23 (5,116,513 rows), `BHelperMatchArm` k=23 (5,670,286), `KMachineReturnRight` k=21 (1,794,327);
  - dispatch selector alone (no fragments): k=22 (2,747,489 rows);
  - 63 existing per-rule fragments total 132,850,191 IR instructions; 45 of 108 rules have no fragment;
  - one dispatch circuit is about 1.27 M instructions for every one of the 108 rules; the cost is in the shared facts block (PROG walk, value reads, 128-bit decompositions), not the per-rule path;
  - so k_U >= 23 measured, about 28-29 ESTIMATE; no S satisfies `k_U + log2 S <= 20`; the leaf prover caps k at 19 today (`crates/mori-backend/src/proving.rs:22`).
  - Also measured: node `SHKIVC06` 652,437 rows over a stand-in leaf and 741,708 over the k=13 C6 digest leaf; run decider 929,166 rows; node step 61-67 s at 16.6-17.6 GB, k=20; a three-slot node is 1,078,147 rows (k=21, F22). Gate G-C needs fact(3) (293 steps) and list123 (303 steps) under 2 h and 48 GB.
  - Decide the leaf architecture that meets GP-1 under these numbers. Candidates include: shrink the shared facts cost (committed memory, lookup arguments, a different value encoding) so one universal leaf fits; per-rule or per-rule-class leaf keys admitted through the GP-3 key registry as named keys; a VM run inline in the node as a processor with continuations; a two-layer design with a different inner proof system. Give the expected k and per-step cost, and how G-C is met.
- **D3 The four GP-3/GP-4 wording points** raised by the architecture study (`research/sherlock-gp-architecture-20261110/architecture.md`): (i) a node that takes two prior proofs plus new work needs inline work or k=21; (ii) circuits outside the Midnight stdlib configuration have no adapter path; (iii) ledger-format (Blake2b transcript) Compact proofs need a new transcript gadget, while stage 1 re-proves with Poseidon; (iv) fixed tree depth versus expandable storage. For each, decide how the design meets the requirement text of `general-purpose.md`, or propose exact wording for an owner amendment with the reason.
- **D4 Inline processor versus separate leaf plus lifts.** The study's dissent: Fable keeps separate leaf proofs plus run/foreign lift proofs under named core keys `{U, R, F, N, C, D}`; Astra wants the VM and the foreign verifiers inline in the node as a processor with continuations (core keys N and D only). Decide, in the light of D2.

`openspec/changes/sherlock-vm-consensus-20261107/general-purpose.md` (GP-1 universal VM; GP-2 cross-run composition; GP-3 foreign proofs through an authenticated key registry; GP-4 any shape, PCD). Read text file `openspec/changes/sherlock-vm-consensus-20261107/general-purpose.md`.
1|# General-purpose and universal recursion: definition
2|
3|Owner decision, 2026-11-10: "It needs to be general purpose recursion. Make sure we understand what that means. And universal". Asked which properties the term must include, the owner selected all four of: universal VM, cross-run composition, foreign proofs, and any shape (PCD).
4|
5|This file defines the target. It replaces every narrower reading of "general purpose" in this change (`design.md` §3.6, SRC-017). Each property names its acceptance test. The gaps list what the code does today.
6|
7|## GP-1 Universal VM
8|
9|One fixed key set proves the execution of every program of the Sherlock language, on every input, for every run length and every outcome. A new program needs no new key, no new contract and no new ceremony.
10|
11|- Programs and inputs are data. The public statement carries `prog_d` (program identity) and `input_d` (run input). Neither is a circuit constant.
12|- Every outcome is a provable statement: `Halted(v)` for every value type (the result as a digest of a canonical value encoding), `Rejected(code)` and `Exhausted(kind)`.
13|- Capacity does not depend on the key. A program whose state does not fit one leaf's carriers runs against committed memory: state lives behind a commitment, and each step proves its reads and writes against it. A fixed ladder of capacity keys is not universal.
14|- The run length is bounded only by the height field (below 2^64).
15|
16|Acceptance: one key set and one deployed verifier contract accept proofs of at least three programs that the key set was not built from, including one program larger than one leaf's carriers, one run with input, and one run of each outcome kind.
17|
18|Gaps today: the keys are bound to one inventory, layout, `Bounds`, profile and S (`design.md` §2.4; `ivc.rs:575`; `run_decider.rs:206-216`). Only `Halted` with a u128 result is accepted (`run_decider.rs:278-288`; `sherlock_c6_witness_stream.rs:138-158`). There is no run input (`sherlock_c6_witness_stream.rs:170-177`). There is one contract per `(program_d, init_d)` (`sherlock-run.compact:25-26,40-47`).
19|
20|## GP-2 Cross-run composition
21|
22|A proven run can be consumed by another proof, and many runs can be combined into one proof.
23|
24|- Consumption: a run can take as input the claim `(prog_d', input_d', outcome_d')` of another verified run, and that claim is checked in-circuit, not trusted.
25|- Batching: independent runs, of the same or different programs, aggregate into one proof whose statement commits to the set of claims.
26|
27|Acceptance: (a) a run of program B whose input is the verified result of a run of program A, accepted once on-chain; (b) one proof that aggregates at least three runs of different programs, accepted once on-chain, from which each claim can be opened.
28|
29|Gap today: linked segments share one `prog_d` (`Aggregation.lean:49`), and the node verifies one fixed leaf key and itself (`ivc.rs:548-562`).
30|
31|## GP-3 Foreign proofs
32|
33|The recursion verifies and aggregates proofs of circuits other than the Sherlock leaf. These include Compact contract circuits and other PLONK/halo2 circuits on the same curve and commitment scheme.
34|
35|- A circuit is admitted by its verifying key, whose identity is a member of an authenticated registry (a commitment to the set of admitted keys). The node proves membership in-circuit; it does not take the key as a constant.
36|- A statement adapter maps each admitted circuit's public inputs to the common claim form.
37|
38|Acceptance: one proof that aggregates a Sherlock run and at least one proof from a Compact contract circuit, both checked in-circuit against the registry, accepted on-chain.
39|
40|Gap today: the node verifies only the fixed leaf key and itself (`ivc.rs:548-562`). There is no key registry and no adapter.
41|
42|## GP-4 Any shape (proof-carrying data)
43|
44|Aggregation is not limited to a linear chain: it covers chains, trees and DAGs of any depth, with a constant-size final proof.
45|
46|- A node can take at least two prior proofs (arity >= 2) plus new work. Every node shape is served by the same key set; there is no per-depth or per-level key.
47|- The shape is bound into the statement, so the verifier knows exactly which claims were combined.
48|- The proof size and the verification cost do not grow with the depth or the number of claims.
49|
50|Acceptance: one key set proves a chain, a balanced tree and a DAG in which one claim feeds two consumers, each at depth >= 8, with the final proof size equal across shapes.
51|
52|Gap today: the shape in use is the linear chain. The uniform three-slot tree node needs k=21 (F22) and is closed (`tasks.md` 5.7; `speed-levers.json`).
53|
54|## Consequences
55|
56|- The consensus design (`design.md`) meets none of GP-1 to GP-4 in full. It is one linear IVC chain over one program under one capacity-bound key set. It remains the first milestone toward GP-1, not the end state.
57|- GP-3 and GP-4 need a node that verifies more than one proof from a registry of keys. The closed tree result (k=21 at arity 3) shows that the node size must be designed for this from the start, for example with accumulation (split accumulation or folding) in place of full in-circuit verification. That is an architecture decision with its own experiments and review.
58|- Every requirement and task in this change is to be checked against GP-1 to GP-4. A narrowing needs an explicit owner decision.

33|### 2.2 Dispatch (one-hot)
34|
35|Today the dispatch owner emits a block for one constant `RuleIdC` and each fragment is its own circuit. In the universal leaf the dispatch is computed once per step:
36|
37|1. Inputs: the pre carriers (IMAGE, HELPER, DATA where a value read is gated on, PROG via the parser walk, CTX).
38|2. Derivation, in the order Core uses (`c6_dispatch_step.rs:9-16`): P0 `outcome == Running`; P1 publication (`Error` control -> `KAdminPublishError`; `Return` at depth 0 -> `KAdminPublishValue`); P2 `remaining_work == 0` -> `KAdminPublishExhausted`; else `owner_select` over helper group, result-reading rule, helper plan entry, legacy group.
39|3. Output: a one-hot vector `sel[r]` over the supported rule set `R` with `sum(sel) == enable` and each `sel[r]` boolean; `sel[r] == 1` iff rule `r`'s guard path holds. Guard paths include every value read the current per-rule blocks make (for example `equal_differ` reads UInt/Bool/type/constructor values, `c6_dispatch_step.rs:750-806`).
40|4. Every fragment `F_r` is emitted once and gated: its constraints are multiplied by `sel[r]`, and it produces a candidate post image `cand_r` in which lanes outside its declared write set equal the pre lanes. The step's post image is the selection `post = sum_r sel[r] * cand_r + (1 - sum_r sel[r]) * pre`. Inactive fragments therefore never constrain the shared post image (astra-2 early correction: a `post == pre` constraint under `1 - sel[r]` would block the selected fragment's writes). Test: two rules with differing write sets on the same class, valid differing writes accepted.
41|5. Two cases are distinct. A *disabled slot* (`enable == 0`, used for padding a short chunk) accepts the constrained identity `post == pre` and contributes zero to `steps`. An *enabled* step whose Core selection is outside the supported set (extension, financial, `XAdtHelperPlan*`, `XAdtHelperBuild*`; `dispatch_supported`, `c6_dispatch_step.rs:29-32`) has no `sel` bit, so `sum(sel) == 0` with `enable == 1` and the leaf refuses (SVM-004).
42|6. `rules_d` (D5; amended 2026-11-10, review C2 and §5 design edit 3). Slot j has the rule lane `rid_j = sum_r sel_j[r] * lane(r)`, where `lane(r)` is the rule lane of `sherlock_c6_child.rs:430-435` (low 128 bits of SHA-256 of the rule id). Because `sum(sel_j) == enable_j`, a disabled slot has `rid_j = 0`. 0 is the reserved disabled-slot id; the inventory freeze (4.4) checks that 0 is not the lane of any rule in `R` and that the lanes of `R` are pairwise distinct. `rules_d = Poseidon(dom("SHK_RULES"), rid_0, ..., rid_{S-1})`: always exactly S lanes in slot order, with no special case for S=1 or for one enabled slot. The earlier wording "for S=1 it is the rule id lane" and SRC-001's "`rules_d == rule` when `steps == 1`" are withdrawn. The node treats `rules_d` as an opaque lane. The leaf derives `rules_d` and `steps`; `h_pre` is bound by the node to the bounded previous height, not by the leaf (astra-2 lane ownership).

44|8. Publication (amended 2026-11-10): a step that publishes (`Halted`, `Rejected`, `Exhausted`) is the last enabled slot: `enable_{j+1} == 1` requires the outcome of `post_j` to be `Running`.

52|### 2.3 S-step leaf
53|
54|A leaf proves `S >= 1` consecutive owner steps on one key. Inside the leaf: `pre_0` is the digested `pre_d`; for `i < S-1`, `post_i == pre_{i+1}` lane by lane; `post_{S-1}` is digested as `post_d`. `steps` is the number of *enabled* owner-step events in the leaf; a short final chunk pads with disabled steps (`enable == 0`, identity on lanes, zero contribution to `steps`). Terminal: a step that publishes (`Halted`, `Rejected`, `Exhausted`) is the last enabled step; later slots are disabled. Charged work and fuel stay inside the state digest; `steps` and `h` are physical counts (ISSUE 5).
55|
56|S rule (amended 2026-11-10, review C3 and §5 design edit 2; replaces the 2026-11-08 (3) rule `k_U + log2 S <= 20`): the leaf is U. S and the worker count are chosen at G-A' from measurements of the complete admitted relation and of the node and decider keyed over a leaf of its arch. `k_U + log2 S <= K_LEAF_MAX` is a first sizing estimate. `K_LEAF_MAX` is the largest leaf k the leaf prover accepts within 16 GB: `K_LEAF_MAX` = [PENDING experiment E4: k=20 leaf prove time and RSS, task 4.11]. The wrapper cap is 19 today (`crates/mori-backend/src/proving.rs:22`, `sherlock_c6_child.rs:868,880`); it is a wrapper constant, not an upstream limit. S >= 8 is the planning target. S=4 may be chosen only with a measured leaf time. S <= 2 does not meet G-C at the measured node step and is a redesign trigger. If no S >= 4 fits, the leaf design is revisited before any key. S is a power of two and at most `S_MAX` = 16 (§3.2(1)). S=1 is the one-enabled-slot case of the same relation, not a separate baseline. The leaf is built with S slots (4.2) and keyed once (4.4). The node-only arithmetic is the table in §3.5. Leaf rows grow about S-fold (`k_leaf = k_U + ceil(log2 S)`), prove time about S x t_step, RSS about S x RSS(k_U); the leaf's private witness holds S copies of the carriers; the measured leaf k, time and RSS at the chosen S are recorded at 4.4 (row A20) and the cap is 16 GB per leaf prover so two or three leaf workers fit beside the node under the 100 GB aggregate (open question Q4).

The normative requirement is UISEC-010: no unauthenticated deferred obligation at genesis. Tests match the chosen semantics: non-neutral refusal for (a); semantic irrelevance of a well-formed ignored carry for (b), without requiring identical folded bytes (ignored inputs may still alter transcript encodings); and invalid-leaf refusal through the final pairing for both. Retaining an unscaled supplied carry requires a separately recorded security argument. Model match: the Quint F20 `accOf` folds no carry for a genesis node (`al = []`); the circuit folds `[trivial, trivial, leaf]`, which equals that fold up to neutral terms. Lean (council fixes, `bd7703f4d`): the node fold is `AccAlgebra.nodeFold b p c l = collapse (accumulate [collapse (scale b p), collapse (scale b c), l])` and the genesis lemma is `genesis_collapse_both` (it replaces `genesis_scale_by_bit`). The circuit realizes `nodeFold` on every accepted witness: `p` is scaled by `not_genesis` and collapsed (`collapse_self`); `c` is constrained to collapsed form at every height (scalar one per side, `constrain_collapsed_carry`, so `collapse c = c` and no second MSM is needed) and to the `trivial_acc` encoding at genesis (`= collapse (scale false c)` by `collapse_scale_false`); the fold and the final collapse are the same. 1|# General-purpose and universal recursion: definition
2|
3|Owner decision, 2026-11-10: "It needs to be general purpose recursion. Make sure we understand what that means. And universal". Asked which properties the term must include, the owner selected all four of: universal VM, cross-run composition, foreign proofs, and any shape (PCD).
4|
5|This file defines the target. It replaces every narrower reading of "general purpose" in this change (`design.md` §3.6, SRC-017). Each property names its acceptance test. The gaps list what the code does today.
6|
7|## GP-1 Universal VM
8|
9|One fixed key set proves the execution of every program of the Sherlock language, on every input, for every run length and every outcome. A new program needs no new key, no new contract and no new ceremony.
10|
11|- Programs and inputs are data. The public statement carries `prog_d` (program identity) and `input_d` (run input). Neither is a circuit constant.
12|- Every outcome is a provable statement: `Halted(v)` for every value type (the result as a digest of a canonical value encoding), `Rejected(code)` and `Exhausted(kind)`.
13|- Capacity does not depend on the key. A program whose state does not fit one leaf's carriers runs against committed memory: state lives behind a commitment, and each step proves its reads and writes against it. A fixed ladder of capacity keys is not universal.
14|- The run length is bounded only by the height field (below 2^64).
15|
16|Acceptance: one key set and one deployed verifier contract accept proofs of at least three programs that the key set was not built from, including one program larger than one leaf's carriers, one run with input, and one run of each outcome kind.
17|
18|Gaps today: the keys are bound to one inventory, layout, `Bounds`, profile and S (`design.md` §2.4; `ivc.rs:575`; `run_decider.rs:206-216`). Only `Halted` with a u128 result is accepted (`run_decider.rs:278-288`; `sherlock_c6_witness_stream.rs:138-158`). There is no run input (`sherlock_c6_witness_stream.rs:170-177`). There is one contract per `(program_d, init_d)` (`sherlock-run.compact:25-26,40-47`).
19|
20|## GP-2 Cross-run composition
21|
22|A proven run can be consumed by another proof, and many runs can be combined into one proof.
23|
24|- Consumption: a run can take as input the claim `(prog_d', input_d', outcome_d')` of another verified run, and that claim is checked in-circuit, not trusted.
25|- Batching: independent runs, of the same or different programs, aggregate into one proof whose statement commits to the set of claims.
26|
27|Acceptance: (a) a run of program B whose input is the verified result of a run of program A, accepted once on-chain; (b) one proof that aggregates at least three runs of different programs, accepted once on-chain, from which each claim can be opened.
28|
29|Gap today: linked segments share one `prog_d` (`Aggregation.lean:49`), and the node verifies one fixed leaf key and itself (`ivc.rs:548-562`).
30|
31|## GP-3 Foreign proofs
32|
33|The recursion verifies and aggregates proofs of circuits other than the Sherlock leaf. These include Compact contract circuits and other PLONK/halo2 circuits on the same curve and commitment scheme.
34|
35|- A circuit is admitted by its verifying key, whose identity is a member of an authenticated registry (a commitment to the set of admitted keys). The node proves membership in-circuit; it does not take the key as a constant.
36|- A statement adapter maps each admitted circuit's public inputs to the common claim form.
37|
38|Acceptance: one proof that aggregates a Sherlock run and at least one proof from a Compact contract circuit, both checked in-circuit against the registry, accepted on-chain.
39|
40|Gap today: the node verifies only the fixed leaf key and itself (`ivc.rs:548-562`). There is no key registry and no adapter.
41|
42|## GP-4 Any shape (proof-carrying data)
43|
44|Aggregation is not limited to a linear chain: it covers chains, trees and DAGs of any depth, with a constant-size final proof.
45|
46|- A node can take at least two prior proofs (arity >= 2) plus new work. Every node shape is served by the same key set; there is no per-depth or per-level key.
47|- The shape is bound into the statement, so the verifier knows exactly which claims were combined.
48|- The proof size and the verification cost do not grow with the depth or the number of claims.
49|
50|Acceptance: one key set proves a chain, a balanced tree and a DAG in which one claim feeds two consumers, each at depth >= 8, with the final proof size equal across shapes.
51|
52|Gap today: the shape in use is the linear chain. The uniform three-slot tree node needs k=21 (F22) and is closed (`tasks.md` 5.7; `speed-levers.json`).
53|
54|## Consequences
55|
56|- The consensus design (`design.md`) meets none of GP-1 to GP-4 in full. It is one linear IVC chain over one program under one capacity-bound key set. It remains the first milestone toward GP-1, not the end state.
57|- GP-3 and GP-4 need a node that verifies more than one proof from a registry of keys. The closed tree result (k=21 at arity 3) shows that the node size must be designed for this from the start, for example with accumulation (split accumulation or folding) in place of full in-circuit verification. That is an architecture decision with its own experiments and review.
58|- Every requirement and task in this change is to be checked against GP-1 to GP-4. A narrowing needs an explicit owner decision.

# Council: advisory cross-family review

Council is the contract for a cross-family review round. It is advisory only.
It does not own release or merge authority.

**Core principle:** actionable dissent creates a correction requirement.
Majority, deadline pressure, and an overall approval never override an
admissible `changes_requested` result. Dissent does not authorize an automatic
second Council round.

## Who does what

The **lead agent** runs the round with the tools that exist now:

- launches lanes with the platform skills: `codex` (OpenAI), `grok` (xAI),
  `agy` (Google), `muse` (Meta), and Claude subagents (Anthropic). Each CLI uses
  its own default sign-in; Council handles no credentials;
- coordinates lanes over `agentbus` when they need to talk or hand off;
- fixes the review bundle, blinds identities, and keeps the identity map;
- classifies results and applies the Council rules below.

Council owns the rules. The owner and the repo's own checks decide merge and
release. See `references/ownership.md`.

## When to use

- Independent cross-provider proposals would reduce single-family bias
- Blinded non-author review of an implementation round is required
- Dissent must stay preserved until each finding is fixed
- A typed abstention is a valid outcome for missing evidence

## When not to use

- Merge or release decisions (the owner and the repo's checks own those)
- A single same-family audit of the implementer (use a cross-vendor audit lane)

## Round (summary)

1. **Write the brief.** One question, the acceptance criteria, and the
   response shape (verdict, findings, evidence). No free-form "thoughts?".
2. **Fix the bundle.** Record `base_sha`, `head_sha`, and
   `git diff base..head | sha256sum`. Responses bind to this triple.
3. **Proposals are independent.** When Council gathers proposals, each lane
   writes its own without seeing the others.
4. **Blind before review.** Strip provider, model, CLI, lane, and author names
   from every candidate. Give each a random id (`cand-7f3a`). Keep the map in a
   file outside every review input. Do not rewrite substance. Record the
   SHA-256 of each blinded prompt file next to the verdict it produced.
5. **Smoke each CLI first.** One short prompt per CLI (for example "Reply with
   exactly: 2" for `1+1`) before the round. A failed smoke is an infrastructure
   problem; fix it, it is not a verdict.
6. **Review by non-authors from other families.** No reviewer reviews its own
   family's work. Pin the `agy` model before you classify its family (see the
   `agy` skill).
7. **Classify transport before reading advice.** Timeout, cancel, signal,
   crash, empty or malformed output, and exit 0 with JSON-looking prose are
   infrastructure failures, not verdicts. Retry them; a retry does not use up
   a correction round.
8. **Count substantive verdicts only.** Closure needs at least three distinct
   completed verdicts (`approved` or `changes_requested`) from at least two
   model families. A completed `insufficient_evidence` abstention is recorded
   but does not count.
9. **Any admissible `changes_requested` blocks.** Record the finding, fix it,
   build a new bundle, and verify the fix with a deterministic check (test,
   diff, re-run). Do not run Council again for the same decision unless the
   owner asks.
10. **Stay advisory.** Council output is a report to the owner or lead. It
    never stands in for the repo's tests, audits, or the owner's merge call.

Full rules: `references/protocol.md`.

## Hard stops

| Stop | Reality |
|---|---|
| "Majority approved, ship it" | One admissible `changes_requested` blocks progress. |
| "Deadline: accept with notes" | Deadline pressure never overrides dissent. |
| "Missing member: treat as approve" | Missing, empty, malformed, infrastructure failure, quorum not met, and abstention are never approval. |
| "Exit 0 plus JSON-looking text is a verdict" | Classify the transport first. Incomplete or cancelled turns are infrastructure failures. |
| "Ancestor of the head is fine" | `base_sha`, `head_sha`, and the diff hash must match exactly. |
| "Leave model names on candidates" | Reviewers see random candidate ids only; the lead keeps the map. |
| "A failed smoke burns a correction round" | Infrastructure retries never use up a correction round. |
| "Run Council again after a fix" | Verify the fix deterministically. A second round needs the owner's say-so. |

## Interfaces

- Codex UI metadata: `agents/openai.yaml`
- Lane launch: the `codex`, `grok`, `agy`, and `muse` skills
- Lane messaging and claims: the `agentbus` skill

25|   model rows at circuits 7.3.0: self + stand-in leaf 652,437; self + self 730,243;
26|   self + self + leaf 1,078,147; self + self + leaf + leaf 1,278,670

341|
342|Node: two slots, each off or one proof under N, R or F. The all-off node is refused. R has a
343|one-leaf mode for odd counts and single-leaf runs. A disabled
344|slot contributes canonical neutral accumulator encodings to the fold (Astra's point; the
345|current genesis handling at `ivc.rs:538-546` is the pattern, and it is why `collapse_self`
346|cannot be removed as a local optimisation).

348|Shape binding has two parts. `set_root` binds the claim DAG by content: `leaf(c) =
349|H(LEAFCLAIM, c)`, `join = H(JOIN, l, r)`, `dep = H(DEP, c_run, deps_root)`. Content addressing
350|identifies equal subgraphs, ignores unary nodes and ignores how a run's segments were
351|bracketed; that is intended for claims and it is not the whole proof graph. `shape_d` binds
352|the proof graph at every R, F and N. Both are in the proved statement, not in an off-chain
353|manifest. Today it is
354|the manifest: the Quint decider "does not read the manifest" and shape binding is "decider plus
355|verify_chain" (`models/sherlock/quint/aggregation.qnt:16-22,464-467`). A SEG carries no shape by
356|design: `link` is associative (`Aggregation.lean:291`) and the bracketing of one run does not
357|change its statement (`same_leaves_same_stmt`, `:708`).
358|
359|DAG fan-out: the SET proof of claim A is the right child of the seal node of B and of the seal
360|node of C. A is proved once and verified twice.

20|## 1. Recommended architecture
21|
22|### 1.1 The facts that decide it
23|
24|1. **The node's cost is the non-native MSM, and three proof slots do not fit k=20.** Measured
25|   model rows at circuits 7.3.0: self + stand-in leaf 652,437; self + self 730,243;
26|   self + self + leaf 1,078,147; self + self + leaf + leaf 1,278,670
27|   (`qa/sherlock/decisions/speed-levers.json:22-29`); self + C6 digest leaf 741,708
28|   (`qa/sherlock/manifests/node.json:22`); decider 929,166
29|   (`qa/sherlock/manifests/run-decider.json:20`). 2^20 = 1,048,576. Two collapses are 78% of the
30|   node (`speed-levers.json:66`). Pairings are already deferred to the decider
31|   (`crates/mori-recursion/src/ivc.rs:10-31`), so "defer the pairings" is not an available gain.
32|2. **The in-circuit verifier is specialised to one constraint system and one k.** `AssignedVk`
33|   keeps `domain` and `cs` off-circuit; only `transcript_repr` is in circuit
34|   (`MC:verifier/mod.rs:55-66`). A Midnight constraint system is a function of
35|   `(ZkStdLibArch, k)` (`ZS:lib.rs:159-209,1573-1586`). ZKIR v3 picks the arch per circuit from
36|   the instructions used, always with `bls12_381: false`, and k by `optimal_k`
37|   (`L:zkir-v3/src/ir_vm.rs:1212-1263`; `L:zkir-v3/src/ir.rs:105-106`). Compact circuits
38|   therefore fall into many `(arch, k)` classes, none of which is the node's
39|   (`crates/mori-recursion/src/lib.rs:23-30`).
40|3. **Ledger proofs use a Blake2b transcript; the gadget verifies Poseidon transcripts only.**
41|   `L:transient-crypto/src/proofs.rs:64-65,563-575`; `MC:verifier/types.rs:144,149,191,196`.
42|   Keys do not depend on the transcript (`transcript_repr` is Blake2b of the key in both cases,
43|   `MP:plonk/mod.rs:255-278`).
44|4. **Fixed-base work is deferred by name, only for keys the decider knows.**
45|   `MC:verifier/msm.rs:14-17,43-53`; `ivc.rs:10-15`. A key chosen by witness from a registry
46|   must have its fixed and permutation commitments witnessed and multiplied in circuit as
47|   variable bases; `resolve_fixed_bases` accepts assigned points (`MC:verifier/msm.rs:491`). One
48|   variable base is 3-4k rows (ESTIMATE, `research/sherlock-speed-replan-20261108/prover.md:155`).
49|5. **Whole-state hashing binds capacity to the key.** The leaf hashes every carrier lane
50|   (`crates/mori-backend/src/sherlock_c6_child.rs:551-569`). Poseidon is width 3, rate 2, 8 full
51|   and 60 partial rounds with 5 skips (`MC:hash/poseidon/constants/mod.rs:17-26`;
52|   `MC:hash/poseidon/poseidon_chip.rs:50`): 18 round rows per permutation, before absorption,
53|   output and encoding rows (a lower bound, not a `cost_model` reading; section 3.3). One carrier side at the holdout draft config is about
54|   35k lanes (`docs/sherlock/stagenet-gp-recursion.md:157-158`).
55|6. **No BLS12-381 curve cycle, and no folding or split-accumulation prover in the pinned
56|   crates.** `research/sherlock-speed-replan-20261108/tree.md:27,111`; the only trace of split
57|   accumulation in midnight-proofs is a comment on an unused field (`MP:plonk/traces.rs:14-18`).

59|### 1.2 The architecture
60|
61|**A binary proof-carrying-data node over the existing KZG accumulation, with typed statements,
62|a claim tree, a key registry, and committed memory in the VM.** Both designers arrive at the
63|same core: one self-recursive node with two predecessor slots at k=20, never three proof slots;
64|claims as the unit of composition; a registry root held by one contract; committed memory;
65|in-circuit genesis. They differ on where new work enters the node (section 3).
66|
67|```
68|L0  base proofs
69|      U    universal Sherlock leaf: S steps over committed state           core key
70|      X    foreign circuits (Compact contract circuits, other PLONK/KZG)  registry, kind = direct
71|      A_c  adapter for one class (arch, k, exact public-input count,
72|           transcript): prepares one X proof under a witnessed key,
73|           publishes [vk_id_inner, out_d, carried accumulator]            registry, kind = adapter
74|L1  lifts (node class: bls12_381 + poseidon, k=20)
75|      R    run lift: verifies one or two U proofs, links them -> SEG      core key, named
76|      F    foreign lift: verifies one adapter-class proof under a
77|           witnessed registry key, folds the adapter's carried
78|           accumulator, proves membership of the adapter key and of
79|           the inner key, emits a claim -> SET                            core key, named
80|L2  node N: two slots; each slot is off or one proof under N, R or F     core key, self-recursive
81|      SEG + SEG -> SEG   adjacent segments of one run
82|      SEG       -> SET   seal: opens post_d; h_lo = 0, terminal outcome, deps_d empty; proves the
83|                         Sherlock leaf identity is a registry member -> one RUN claim
84|      SEG + SET -> SET   seal with dependencies (the opened deps_d equals the SET root)
85|      SET + SET -> SET   join
86|L3  closing proof C (node class): verifies the root N proof, resolves the named bases of
87|    N, R and F, collapses                                                 core key
88|    decider D (k=20, Blake2b transcript, ledger template): verifies C, checks the pairing,
89|    exposes [reg_root, set_root, n_claims, shape_d]                       core key, on chain
90|L4  contract SherlockClaims: acceptRoot, openClaim, admitKey
91|```
92|
93|Statements.
94|
95|| Layer | Statement |
96||---|---|
97|| U | `[binding, prog_d, input_d, pre_d, post_d, h_pre, steps, deps_d]`. `pre_d` and `post_d` digest a fixed register file plus memory commitments. The leaf with `h_pre = 0` proves `pre = Init(prog_d, input_d)` in circuit. |
98|| SEG | `(leaf_id, prog_d, input_d, pre_d, post_d, h_lo, h_hi)`: the `Seg` of `clean/fork/Clean/Sherlock/Aggregation.lean:27` plus `input_d` and the leaf identity. |
99|| claim | `c = H(CLAIM, kind, id, in_d, out_d)`. RUN: `id = prog_d`, `in_d = input_d`, `out_d = H(outcome_kind, value_d, n_steps)`. FOREIGN: `id = vk_id`, `out_d = H(public inputs)`. |
100|| SET | `(set_root, n_claims)`. `set_root` is the hash of the claim DAG with domain-separated tags (claim leaf, JOIN, DEP); `n_claims` counts occurrences, not distinct claims. |
101|| every R, F, N statement | also `shape_d = H(SHAPE, relation tag, slot bits, child shape_d values, local statement)`: the proof graph itself, including segment bracketing and unary nodes (Astra's separation of shape from claim content, adopted; section 3.3). |
102|| N | `[n_repr, r_repr, f_repr, reg_root, tag, payload, shape_d, acc]`. A node requires its children to carry the same three key representations and the same `reg_root`. R and F statements end with their own carried accumulator, which the parent folds. |
103|| D | public values `[reg_root, set_root, n_claims, shape_d]` in the `acceptRoot` transcript template. |
104|
105|Key set: `{U, R, F, N, C, D}`, fixed and independent of program, input, run length, memory
106|size, registry content, shape and depth. Programs, inputs, registry members (foreign keys and
107|adapter keys) and the shape are data.
108|
109|How the node takes R and F without a third slot or an in-circuit MSM over their keys. The
110|decider already resolves the node's own fixed bases by name. R and F do not verify N, so they
111|are keyed first and N takes their `transcript_repr` as public inputs, as it takes its own
112|(`MC:verifier/verifier_gadget.rs:207`). R, F and N are all node-class relations at k=20, so one
113|verifier instance per slot serves all three (fact 2). In a slot, the witnessed representation
114|is constrained to one of the three by a one-hot selector, and each deferred fixed-base scalar is
115|recorded under the selected name set. The transcript absorbs the key representation first
116|(`MC:verifier/verifier_gadget.rs:296`), so a proof made under one key does not verify under
117|another. C resolves the three name sets with constant bases. The accumulation challenge hashes
118|accumulator encodings, which do not contain names (`MC:verifier/msm.rs:229-290`), so the
119|routing is sound only with the full set of constraints listed in section 3.1 item 3; the
120|library does not enforce them.
121|
122|### 1.3 How each requirement is met
123|
124|- **GP-1 universal VM.** U is keyed over the rule inventory and a fixed register file, not
125|  over `Bounds`. `prog_d` is a commitment to the program table and `input_d` a commitment to the
126|  input and execution parameters; both are opened in circuit. Frames are a hash chain, the
127|  append-only data arena and the program table are Merkle trees. Every outcome kind is a
128|  terminal state that the seal rule opens and turns into `out_d`. Height is range-checked below 2^64
129|  (exists, `ivc.rs` `constrain_heights`). Acceptance: three unseen programs, one above the old
130|  carrier size, one with input, one of each outcome kind, one key set, one contract.
131|- **GP-2 cross-run composition.** A sealed run is a claim. Batching is `SET + SET`; each claim
132|  opens from `set_root` by a Merkle path (`openClaim`). Consumption: a run's state carries
133|  `deps_d`, the commitment to the claims it consumed; the seal-with-dependencies rule requires a
134|  verified SET whose root equals it.
135|- **GP-3 foreign proofs.** The registry is a Poseidon Merkle root in contract state. The
136|  Sherlock leaf is a registry entry too (kind `run`, identity from U's key representation and
137|  the machine version, carried as a lane of every SEG): the seal rule proves its membership, so
138|  that the run and the foreign proof are "both checked in-circuit against the registry" as the
139|  GP-3 acceptance test says. U stays a constant of R; the path is a policy check, not key
140|  selection. F takes
141|  the adapter key by witness, computes its identity, proves its membership and the inner key's
142|  membership against `reg_root`, and folds both the adapter proof's obligation and the inner
143|  proof's carried obligation. Adapters map public inputs to the claim form. A Compact circuit
144|  enters through the adapter of its class.
145|- **GP-4 any shape.** One node key, two slots, any nesting, any depth. A proof is data and can
146|  be an input to two parents, which gives DAG fan-out. `set_root` binds which claims were combined and how; `shape_d` binds the proof graph. The
147|  final object is always one decider proof.
148|
149|### 1.4 What is not met as written, and the closest design
150|
151|No evidence shows that a requirement is impossible on this stack, and none needs a different
152|proof system on present evidence. Nothing is measured for the new relations either: every row
153|figure for N, R, F, C and the adapters is an ESTIMATE until experiment 1 and 2 run. Four points
154|where the recommended design does not meet the text as written:
155|
156|1. **"A node can take at least two prior proofs (arity >= 2) plus new work"** (GP-4). In the
157|   recommended design a k=20 node takes two proofs, each either prior (N) or new (R, F); two
158|   prior proofs plus new work is two nodes. Three verifier slots are 1,078,147 rows (fact 1).
159|   The designs that meet the sentence in one node: (a) Astra's inline work, constraints of the
160|   node itself beside two self slots, within what is left of 2^20 after about 730k rows; (b) a
161|   three-slot node at k=21 at about twice the node cost, which needs an SRS above 2^20 (only
162|   `bls_midnight_2p20` is in the local parameter cache; GP-4 does not fix k). Experiment 1
163|   measures (a) beside the named lifts. Astra holds that the two-node reading is a narrowing
164|   and must not be put to the owner as an interpretation (section 3.2 dissent 1).
165|2. **"Other PLONK/halo2 circuits on the same curve and commitment scheme"** (GP-3). The
166|   verifier circuit is a function of the foreign circuit's constraint system (fact 2) and of
167|   its exact public-input count, because the count is absorbed into the transcript as a
168|   circuit constant (`MP:plonk/verifier.rs:68-74`; `MC:verifier/verifier_gadget.rs:303-306`).
169|   The recommended design therefore needs one adapter key per class `(arch, k, public-input
170|   count, transcript)`, and covers circuits built with the Midnight stdlib configuration: two
171|   instance columns, one committed and one ordinary (`ZS:lib.rs:547-548`), and one challenge
172|   phase (`MC:verifier/verifier_gadget.rs:308-310`). Adapter keys are registry data; both
173|   designers now read them as compatible with the fixed core key set. A halo2 circuit outside
174|   that configuration, or over another SRS, has no path in the recommended design. The design
175|   that covers it is Astra's verifier program run by an in-node processor (section 3.2
176|   dissent 2); it is built nowhere and unmeasured.
177|3. **A proof already accepted on Midnight** (ledger bytes, no witness). Stage 1 verifies a
178|   Poseidon-transcript proof of the same Compact circuit under the same deployed key, which
179|   needs the witness holder. Ledger bytes need the keyed Blake2b transcript with its prefixes
180|   (`MP:transcript/implementors.rs:13-24`), complete parsing (`ZS:utils/plonk_api.rs:154`) and
181|   the point checks the recursive gadget leaves out
182|   (`MC:verifier/transcript_gadget.rs:70-80,118-128`). The stdlib Blake2b wrapper is unkeyed
183|   (`ZS:external/blake2b.rs:101`) and enabling its chip changes the adapter's arch. The row
184|   cost is unmeasured (experiment 3). Astra holds that GP-3 is not complete before this works
185|   (section 3.2 dissent 3).
186|4. **"Capacity does not depend on the key"** (GP-1). Fixed Merkle depths are a capacity fixed
187|   by the relation. With depth equal to the machine's address width the bound is the address
188|   space, as the height bound is 2^64; Astra holds that this is still a narrowing and that
189|   storage must be expandable with paths processed across proofs (section 3.2 dissent 4).
190|
191|Also open, and not a stack limit: no concrete security bound exists for arbitrary-depth PCD
192|with this accumulation. The Lean model takes accumulation validity as a premise
193|(`Aggregation.lean:1230-1244`), and known PCD analyses "incur expensive blowups" with depth
194|unless the SNARK has a straightline extractor (https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/1646). A balanced
195|tree has depth log M where the chain has depth M.

279|### 2.3 Q3 Registry and adapters
280|
281|Key identity: `vk_id = H(VK, class_id, transcript_repr, comm_d)`, with `class_id = H(arch, k,
282|exact public-input count, proof and key format version, transcript id, srs id)` and `comm_d` the Poseidon digest of the fixed and
283|permutation commitments in key order. It is a deterministic function of the key bytes, so
284|anyone can recompute it from a deployed Midnight key (`ZS:lib.rs:1537-1562` for the layout).
285|The public-input count is in `MidnightVK` and not in `transcript_repr`, so it must be bound
286|here (Astra's finding; verified). F does not recompute Blake2b; the binding of
287|`transcript_repr` to `comm_d` is as strong as admission, so admission must check that the
288|tuple is the normalization of real key bytes, by governance or by an admission proof.
289|The SRS identity is part of the class because the pairing equation is specific to one SRS
290|(`MP:poly/kzg/params.rs:235-237`; Astra's point, adopted): a key over another SRS cannot be
291|accumulated with ours.
292|
293|Registry: Poseidon Merkle tree of `H(REG, vk_id, kind)`, kind in {direct, adapter, run};
294|root in contract state; `admitKey` appends. A direct key is a foreign circuit: the claim about
295|it has `id = vk_id`, which the adapter computes from the witnessed key and F checks against the
296|registry. An adapter key may emit FOREIGN claims about direct keys. A run entry is a Sherlock
297|leaf identity allowed to emit RUN claims: U at first; a different leaf prover later would be a
298|second run entry and would enter through F. Adapter and run entries make claims on behalf of
299|other identities and need governed admission; an adapter key can be checked by regenerating
300|it from its class. Admitting an adapter does not admit the circuits it can verify: F also
301|proves that the adapter's `vk_id_inner` is a registry member (round 1 omitted this; section
302|3.3). Whether a proof made under an older `reg_root` stays usable after an admission is a
303|policy choice: current root only, or an authenticated root history with a revocation rule.
304|

12|## 0. Six facts that decide the design
13|
14|F-1. **The in-circuit verifier is specialised to one constraint system and one k.** `AssignedVk`
15|holds `domain` and `cs` off-circuit; "the only in-circuit field is the `transcript_repr`"
16|(`MC:verifier/mod.rs:55-66`). A slot whose key is chosen by witness therefore works only across
17|keys that share the constraint system and the domain.
18|
19|F-2. **A Midnight constraint system is a function of `(ZkStdLibArch, k)`.** `MidnightVK::read`
20|rebuilds it with `ZkStdLib::configure(&mut cs, (architecture, k - 1))` (`ZS:lib.rs:1573-1586`);
21|the arch is 13 chip flags plus `nr_pow2range_cols` (`ZS:lib.rs:159-209`). ZKIR v3 picks the arch
22|per circuit from the instructions used (jubjub, poseidon, sha2_256, keccak_256, secp256k1, p256,
23|curve25519; `bls12_381: false`, `nr_pow2range_cols: 4`; `L:zkir-v3/src/ir_vm.rs:1212-1263`) and k
24|by `optimal_k` (`L:zkir-v3/src/ir.rs:105-106`; `ZS:lib.rs:2122`). So Compact circuits fall into
25|many `(arch, k)` classes, and none of them is the node's class (`bls12_381 + poseidon`,
26|`crates/mori-recursion/src/lib.rs:23-30`).
27|
28|F-3. **Ledger proofs use a Blake2b transcript; the gadget verifies Poseidon transcripts only.**
29|`pub type TranscriptHash = blake2b_simd::State` (`L:transient-crypto/src/proofs.rs:64-65`), used
30|by `IrSource::prove` (`L:zkir-v3/src/ir.rs:82-102`) and `VerifierKey::verify`
31|(`L:transient-crypto/src/proofs.rs:563-575`). The gadget's `SelfEmulation::Hash` is
32|`PoseidonState` for both emulations (`MC:verifier/types.rs:144,149,191,196`). A proof taken from
33|a Midnight transaction cannot enter the node as it is. The key is transcript-independent (keygen
34|uses no transcript; `transcript_repr` is always Blake2b of the key, `MP:plonk/mod.rs:255-278`),
35|so the same Compact circuit can be proved again under its deployed key with a Poseidon
36|transcript by whoever holds the witness.
37|
38|F-4. **Fixed-base work is deferred by name, and only for keys the decider knows.** A partial MSM
39|keeps fixed-base terms as scalars; "the bases are assumed to be fixed and globally known"
40|(`MC:verifier/msm.rs:14-17,43-53`). The node leaves its own fixed-base scalars unresolved and
41|"whoever pins the node key (the decider) resolves them"; the leaf key is a constant and its bases
42|are resolved in circuit (`crates/mori-recursion/src/ivc.rs:10-15`). A key taken from a registry by
43|witness has neither route: its fixed and permutation commitments must be witnessed as points,
44|hashed to the registry leaf, and multiplied in circuit as variable bases. `prover.md:155` puts
45|one variable base at 3-4k rows (ESTIMATE in that file).
46|
47|F-5. **Measured rows at 7.3.0** (`qa/sherlock/decisions/speed-levers.json:22-30`;
48|`qa/sherlock/manifests/node.json`): node self + stand-in leaf 652,437; self + C6 digest leaf
49|741,708; self + self 730,243; self + self + leaf 1,078,147; self + self + leaf + leaf 1,278,670;
50|decider 929,166 (`qa/sherlock/manifests/run-decider.json:20`). 2^20 = 1,048,576. Two collapses are 78% of the node
51|(`speed-levers.json:66`, "collapse_self 239,577 + collapse_final 267,514"). Marginal slot costs
52|from these numbers: second leaf slot +200,523; first leaf slot on a self-self node +347,904.
53|
54|F-6. **Hashing state is what binds capacity to the key.** The leaf hashes every carrier lane
55|(`crates/mori-backend/src/sherlock_c6_child.rs:551-569`, per `review.md` C5). Poseidon here is
56|width 3, rate 2, 8 full + 60 partial rounds with 5 skips (`MC:hash/poseidon/constants/mod.rs:17-26`;
57|`MC:hash/poseidon/poseidon_chip.rs:50`): 18 rows per permutation, 9 rows per absorbed lane
58|(ESTIMATE from the round counts; not a `cost_model` reading). At the holdout draft config one
59|carrier side is about 35k lanes (`docs/sherlock/stagenet-gp-recursion.md:157-158`): about 315k
60|rows per side per step (ESTIMATE), before any VM logic.

62|## 1. Recommended architecture (one page)
63|
64|Name: **typed PCD over KZG accumulation, with named lifts and a claim tree.** It keeps the
65|proof system (midnight-proofs PLONK/KZG, in-circuit verifier with deferred pairing) and changes
66|the node from "self + one constant leaf" to "two polymorphic slots over a fixed set of named core
67|keys", moves every non-core proof behind a lift circuit, and replaces whole-state hashing in the
68|leaf with committed memory.
69|
70|```
71|L0  base proofs (any number of keys, all in the registry or core)
72|      U    universal Sherlock leaf: S steps over committed state        [core key]
73|      X_c  foreign circuits (Compact contract circuits, other PLONK)   [registry, kind=direct]
74|      A_c  adapter per (arch, k) class: verifies one X_c proof under a
75|           witnessed key, emits a common-form claim                    [registry, kind=adapter]
76|L1  lifts (node class: bls12_381 + poseidon, k=20; core keys, named in N and D)
77|      R    run lift: verifies 2 leaf proofs of U (constant key), links them -> SEG
78|      F    foreign lift: verifies 1 node-class proof under a witnessed key,
79|           resolves its fixed bases in circuit, proves registry membership -> SET
80|L2  node N (one key, self-recursive, 2 slots; each slot is one of {N, R, F}, or off)
81|      SEG + SEG -> SEG      (adjacent segments of one run; Lean `link`)
82|      SEG       -> SET      (seal: canonical genesis and terminal outcome -> one RUN claim)
83|      SEG + SET -> SET      (seal with dependencies: the run's `deps_root` equals the SET root)
84|      SET + SET -> SET      (join: root = H(JOIN, left, right))
85|L3  decider D (k=20, Blake2b transcript, ledger template): verifies the last N proof, resolves
86|    the named bases of N, R and F, checks the pairing, exposes [reg_root, set_root, n_claims]
87|L4  one contract `SherlockClaims`: `acceptRoot`, `openClaim`, `admitKey`
88|```
89|
90|Statements.
91|
92|- Leaf U: `[binding, prog_d, input_d, pre_d, post_d, h_pre, steps, deps_d]`. `pre_d`, `post_d`
93|  are digests of a small register file plus memory commitments (section 3). The first leaf
94|  (`h_pre == 0`) proves in circuit that the pre-state is `Init(prog_d, input_d)`.
95|- SEG: `(prog_d, input_d, pre_d, post_d, h_lo, h_hi)`. The `Seg` of `Aggregation.lean:27` plus
96|  `input_d`.
97|- Claim: `c = H(CLAIM, kind, id, in_d, out_d)`. RUN claim: `id = prog_d`, `in_d = input_d`,
98|  `out_d = H(outcome_kind, value_d, n_steps)`. FOREIGN claim: `id = vk_id`, `in_d = 0`,
99|  `out_d = H(public inputs)`.
100|- SET: `(set_root, n_claims)`; `set_root` is the hash of the aggregation DAG itself, with
101|  domain-separated node tags (JOIN, DEP, leaf claim). The shape is the statement.
102|- Node public inputs: `[n_repr, r_repr, f_repr, reg_root, tag, payload(6), acc]`. `n_repr`,
103|  `r_repr`, `f_repr` are the transcript representations of the three named keys; children must
104|  carry the same three values and the same `reg_root`; the decider pins all three.
105|
106|Key set (fixed, program-independent): `{U, R, F, N, D}`. Everything else is data: programs
107|(`prog_d`), inputs, registry members (foreign keys, adapter keys), the shape.
108|
109|How each requirement is met.
110|
111|- **GP-1.** U is keyed over the rule inventory and a fixed register file, not over `Bounds`.
112|  Program and input are opened from commitments; memory is committed (hash-chained stack,
113|  Merkle arena and program table); all three outcome kinds are sealed as `out_d`. Capacity is
114|  bounded by address width, not by the key.
115|- **GP-2.** A sealed run is a claim. Batching is `SET + SET`. Consumption is `SEG + SET` with
116|  `deps_root` carried in the run state; each claim is opened from `set_root` by a Merkle path.
117|- **GP-3.** The registry is a Poseidon Merkle root held by the contract. F proves membership in
118|  circuit and takes the key by witness. Adapters map public inputs to the claim form. A Compact
119|  circuit enters through the adapter of its `(arch, k)` class, as a Poseidon-transcript proof
120|  under its deployed key (stage 1) or as the on-chain Blake2b proof through a transcoding
121|  adapter (stage 2).
122|- **GP-4.** One node key, two slots, any nesting. A proof can be an input to two parents, so a
123|  DAG needs no extra mechanism. The final proof is always one decider proof.

125|What cannot be met as written, and the closest design.
126|
127|1. **"A node can take at least two prior proofs plus new work"** in a single node at k=20: no.
128|   Three verifier slots measure 1,078,147 rows (F-5). The recommended node takes two proofs, each
129|   either prior (N) or new (R, F); a three-input step is two nodes. The literal reading is
130|   available as fallback B (one three-slot node at k=21, section 2). Whether two binary steps
131|   satisfy the sentence is an owner question; the GP-4 acceptance test (chain, tree, DAG at depth
132|   >= 8, one key set, equal proof size) is met either way.
133|2. **"Other PLONK/halo2 circuits on the same curve"** without a per-class adapter key: no. The
134|   verifier circuit is a function of the verified circuit's constraint system (F-1). The closest
135|   design is one adapter key per `(arch, k)` class, generated mechanically from one generic
136|   relation and admitted to the registry like any other key. Core keys and the contract do not
137|   change. Whether adapter keys count against "one key set" is an owner question. Circuits that
138|   break the gadget's assumptions (more than one instance column or challenge phase,
139|   `MC:verifier/verifier_gadget.rs:16-20`) need gadget work before any adapter exists.
140|3. **A proof already posted on Midnight** (third-party, no witness): not in stage 1 (F-3). It
141|   needs an in-circuit Blake2b transcript, which the gadget does not have; the stdlib has a
142|   Blake2b chip (`ZS:lib.rs:186-187`), so this is engineering with an unmeasured row cost
143|   (experiment X6), not a stack limit.
144|
145|No requirement needs a different proof system. Folding or a STARK is an optional later
146|replacement for the leaf prover only (section 2).

149|
150|| Option | Node rows / k | Final proof | Prover cost per node | In 0.8.3 / 7.3.0 | Call |

157|| E. Inner STARK or folding layer, outer KZG wrap | wrap circuit ESTIMATE >= 2^20-2^22 rows of Poseidon for a FRI verifier | decider | fast inner | nothing | Rejected now; same remark as D. |

160|Why A works. The decider already resolves the node's own bases by name. Nothing limits that to
161|one name. R and F do not verify N, so there is no key cycle: R and F are keyed first, N takes
162|their `transcript_repr` as public inputs exactly as it takes its own
163|(`assign_vk_as_public_input`, `MC:verifier/verifier_gadget.rs:207`), and D pins the three
164|values and resolves three sets of constant bases. R, F and N must share one constraint system
165|and k (F-1), which holds when all three are node-class relations at k=20. In a slot, the
166|witnessed `transcript_repr` is constrained to be `b_N*n_repr + b_R*r_repr + b_F*f_repr` with a
167|one-hot `(b_N, b_R, b_F)`, and each deferred scalar `s_j` is written under name set N, R or F as
168|`b_x * s_j`. That is native multiplication only.
169|
170|Why not D for the node. GP-3 inputs are PLONK/KZG proofs. A folding scheme folds instances of
171|one relation; to bring a foreign proof in, the folded step circuit must contain the PLONK
172|verifier, which is the same non-native MSM that fills the node today. Folding removes the
173|recursion overhead only for work that is native to the folded relation (VM steps). Its decider
174|on this stack must also prove the folded witness commitment opens correctly inside a circuit
175|that the stock Midnight verifier accepts, which means an in-circuit pairing for a KZG opening
176|over the whole folded witness; Mira (https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/2025) is the closest
177|published work on folding pairing-based arguments and has no implementation on this stack.
178|Because any node-class proof can enter through F, a folded-run prover can be added later as a
179|registry member that emits RUN claims, without touching the core keys.
180|
181|What R costs. R = {leaf, leaf} with a constant leaf key: ESTIMATE 650-800k rows from
182|self + leaf 652,437-741,708 (one of the two slots there is a self slot with deferred bases, so R
183|is somewhat larger; it depends on the leaf arch, as the +89,271-row step from the stand-in to
184|the C6 leaf key shows). F = one verification plus witnessed-key resolution plus a registry
185|path: ESTIMATE 550-700k. Both need a row probe (X1).
186|
187|Throughput against today's chain (ESTIMATE, node step 61-67 s): a run of M leaves needs M/2 R
188|proofs and M/2 - 1 merge nodes, about M node-class proofs, the same count as the chain, and
189|they are independent, so P workers divide the wall time. Proof size and decider time are
190|unchanged.
191|
192|Soundness note. Depth: known PCD analyses "incur expensive blowups" with depth unless the SNARK
193|has a straightline extractor (https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/1646). A balanced tree has depth
194|log M where the chain has depth M (`tree.md` F6). The accumulation is the BCMS pattern
195|(https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/499).

197|## 3. Q2: universal VM (GP-1)
198|
199|Principle: the leaf sees a fixed-size register file and commitments; everything of unbounded
200|size is behind a commitment that the step opens where it reads or writes.
201|
202|State digest `sd = H(SD, control registers, outcome, fuel and counters, stack_h, arena_root,
203|arena_len, env handle, deps_d)`; `prog_d = H(PROG, prog_root, profile, rule inventory id)`;
204|`input_d = H(IN, input value digest, fuel, stack limit, deps_root)`.
205|
206|| Structure (current carrier) | Commitment | Cost per access (ESTIMATE, 18 rows per Poseidon permutation) |
207||---|---|---|
208|| Program table (PROG section, immutable) | Merkle root `prog_root`, depth 20 | read: 20 permutations = 360 rows |
209|| Frames (13 lanes each, a stack) | hash chain: `stack_h' = H(frame, stack_h)`; top K frames in registers | push or pop: 7 permutations for 13 lanes = 126 rows |
210|| Data arena (append-only, child before parent; `D/design.md` §2.1 `StepInv`) | append-only Merkle tree, depth 32, with `arena_len` | read: 576 rows; append: 1,152 rows |
211|| Environment | persistent structure in the arena (a pointer), or its own Merkle map | as arena |
212|| Helper cursors, value slots in use | registers | 0 |
213|
214|Why Merkle and hash chains and not a lookup or multiset memory argument. A permutation or
215|LogUp memory argument needs a challenge drawn after the whole access log is committed. In a PCD
216|of arbitrary shape and unbounded length there is no such point. A multiset hash into a curve
217|(https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.06502) needs no challenge and is additive, so it would compose; it
218|costs about one hash-to-curve per record and needs a final sweep over every touched cell and a
219|linear-use discipline. It is the cheaper alternative if Merkle paths dominate the leaf (X3
220|decides). Merkle and hash-chain state is local: any segment is provable from `pre_d` alone, in
221|any order and in parallel, which is what trees need. RISC Zero's continuations use the same
222|split, paged memory with Merkle page-in and page-out per segment
223|(https://dev.risczero.com/api/zkvm/optimization).
224|
225|No per-program key: the rule inventory and the register file fix the relation. A program is a
226|Merkle root; a run length is a height below 2^64 (range checks exist, `ivc.rs` `constrain_heights`).
227|A program "larger than one leaf's carriers" does not exist as a category any more.
228|
229|Outcomes. The terminal step writes `(outcome_kind, value_d)`; `value_d` is the digest of the
230|canonical value encoding (for a structured value, its arena root and handle). The seal rule in N
231|requires `outcome_kind != Running` and emits `out_d`. `Rejected(code)` and `Exhausted(kind)` are
232|ordinary terminal states.
233|
234|Genesis. With committed memory the initial state is a few constants plus `prog_root` and
235|`input_d`, so the first leaf can prove `pre == Init(prog_d, input_d)` in circuit at a cost of one
236|state hash. This closes dissent 2 of `review.md` 4.2 in favour of the in-circuit mechanism.
237|
238|Cost against today. A step that makes a program read, 2 arena reads, 1 arena append and 1
239|frame push costs about 360 + 1,152 + 1,152 + 126 = 2,790 rows of hashing (ESTIMATE), against
240|about 630k rows for hashing two 35k-lane sides at the holdout config (F-6) and about 1.7k rows
241|at the 96-lane qualification config. The per-rule logic cost is still unknown (4.1a is running).
242|
243|Risk: this replaces the `sherlock-c6-phys/1` carrier model for unbounded sections. The
244|fragments read lanes of the bounded image today. How much of each fragment survives depends on
245|how many distinct cells a rule touches (X2).
246|
247|## 4. Q3: registry and adapters (GP-3)
248|
249|Key identity. `vk_id = H(VK, class_id, transcript_repr, comm_d)` where `class_id = H(arch, k,
250|n_public_inputs_cap)` and `comm_d` is the Poseidon digest of the fixed and permutation
251|commitments in key order. `transcript_repr` already binds the commitments, the domain and the
252|constraint system by Blake2b (`MP:plonk/mod.rs:255-278`); `comm_d` is there because the circuit
253|needs the points and cannot recompute Blake2b cheaply. `vk_id` is a deterministic function of
254|the key bytes, so anyone can recompute it from a deployed Midnight verifier key.
255|
256|Registry. A Poseidon Merkle tree of leaves `H(REG, vk_id, kind)`, `kind` in {direct, adapter,
257|run-prover}. The root `reg_root` is contract state. `admitKey` appends. Admission policy is the
258|owner's choice: governance key, or permissionless for `direct` (a direct key can only make
259|claims about itself) and governed for `adapter` and `run-prover` (they make claims on behalf of
260|other identities).
261|
262|In circuit (lift F). F witnesses the node-class key's commitments, computes `comm_d` and
263|`vk_id`, proves the Merkle path to `reg_root`, verifies the proof with the gadget, resolves the
264|fixed bases as variable bases (F-4), and emits the claim: for `direct`, `id = vk_id` (computed,
265|cannot be forged); for `adapter`, `id` and `out_d` are read from the adapter's public inputs.
266|
267|Adapters. `A_c` is a node-class relation, generic over `(arch, k)`, that verifies one class-c
268|proof under a witnessed key, computes that key's `vk_id`, hashes its public inputs to `out_d`
269|and exposes `[vk_id_inner, out_d]`. Its key is reproducible by anyone from `(arch, k)`, so its
270|admission can be checked by recomputation. Public inputs: the instance polynomial is evaluated
271|in circuit, linear in the number of inputs; each adapter fixes a cap (for example 1,024) and
272|shorter statements are zero-padded. The ledger limit is 65,536 per call
273|(`L:onchain-runtime/src/transcript.rs:87` per `review.md` C7); an adapter at that cap is a
274|separate, large class.
275|
276|Compact contract proofs. Yes, with two qualifications. (1) Format: a ledger proof is the stdlib
277|PLONK proof under `MidnightVK` (arch, k, public-input count, key; `ZS:lib.rs:1537-1562`) with a
278|Blake2b transcript (F-3). Stage 1 verifies a Poseidon-transcript proof of the same circuit under
279|the same key; the statement proved, "this circuit accepts these public inputs", is identical.
280|Stage 2 adds a Blake2b transcript gadget to the adapter. (2) The repository has verified
281|ZKIR-compiled children in circuit before (the C6 leaf is a ZKIR relation with a Poseidon
282|transcript, `qa/sherlock/manifests/c6-leaf.json`), so the gadget handles ZKIR arch classes. What
283|a Compact proof means to a consumer is its public-input vector (the communication commitment
284|and the transcript of ledger operations); the adapter does not interpret it, it commits to it.
285|
286|Cost of the path for one foreign proof: adapter proof (k=20 class, one verification with
287|in-circuit bases) then F (one verification with in-circuit bases) then a node slot. Two
288|node-class proofs before aggregation. Sherlock leaves skip this through R.
289|
290|## 5. Q4: PCD shape (GP-4)
291|
292|Node: two slots, each `off` or one proof under N, R or F. Rules in section 1. The all-off node
293|is refused. A single-child node is allowed (`unary_left`, `Aggregation.lean:451`).
294|
295|Shape binding. `set_root` is defined by structural recursion: `leaf(c) = H(LEAFCLAIM, c)`,
296|`join = H(JOIN, l, r)`, `dep = H(DEP, c_run, deps_root)`. Two different DAGs give different
297|roots under collision resistance; the verifier learns the exact combination. A SEG carries no
298|shape, by design: `link` is associative (`link_assoc`, `Aggregation.lean:291`) and
299|`same_leaves_same_stmt` (`:708`) says the bracketing of a run does not matter. The shape that
300|GP-4 asks to bind is the shape over claims.
301|
302|DAG fan-out. A proof is data. The same SET proof for claim A can be the right child of the
303|seal node of B and of the seal node of C. A is proved once and verified twice. If B and C are
304|later joined, A's sub-root appears twice in `set_root`; that is a true statement about the DAG.
305|
306|Constant size. Every N proof has the same public-input length; the decider proof is the final
307|object in every shape.
308|
309|Linear and reusable objects. Steps of one run are linear: each height is covered exactly once.
310|That is the existing `Covers` and `linkAll_covers` (`Aggregation.lean:787,858`) and Quint I3
311|(`aggregation.qnt:410`); SEG merging keeps them unchanged because adjacency
312|(`left.post == right.pre`, `left.hi == right.lo`) makes a repeat or a gap unprovable. Claims are
313|facts and are reusable. On-chain acceptance is linear again, by the contract's set of accepted
314|roots.
315|
316|Unique genesis. Today the decider checks the root starts at height 0 from `init_d` (Quint I6,
317|`aggregation.qnt:441`; `non_genesis_refused`, `Aggregation.lean:1106`). In the new node the seal
318|rule does it: `h_lo == 0` and the leaf's in-circuit `Init` check. `result_unique`
319|(`Aggregation.lean:1136`) then reads: for a given `(prog_d, input_d)` there is one RUN claim.
320|
321|Model extensions needed: a claim layer above `Seg` (inductive `SetCert` with join, dep, seal),
322|the theorem "every claim under a decided `set_root` is sound" by induction, shape injectivity,
323|and in Quint a second linear resource (accepted roots) plus the fan-out scenario.
324|
325|## 6. Q5: on-chain fit
326|
327|One contract for all programs, `SherlockClaims`:
328|
329|- state: `reg_root: Field`, `roots: Set<Field>`, optionally `claims: Set<Field>`.
330|- `acceptRoot(set_root, n)`: verifier key = decider D (the same "hand-written key behind a
331|  Compact template" mechanism as `acceptRun`, `tools/sherlock-sdk/sherlock-run.compact:1-15`).
332|  The template reads `reg_root` from the ledger so the decider binds the proof to the current
333|  registry, as `acceptRun` does for `program_d` (`:40-47`); refuses a root already in `roots`.
334|- `openClaim(set_root, claim fields, path)`: an ordinary Compact circuit; proves a Merkle path
335|  from the claim to an accepted root and publishes the claim. Requires the claim tree to use
336|  the hash Compact exposes as `transientHash` (Poseidon in the stdlib arch,
337|  `L:zkir-v3/src/ir_vm.rs:1212-1263`); parameter equality with `MC:hash/poseidon` must be
338|  checked (X7).
339|- `admitKey(vk_id, kind)`: registry append under the admission policy.
340|
341|Limits. Decider key 2,217 B against 50,000 (`review.md` C7); public inputs: about 70 today, far
342|under 65,536; three circuits against 256 per contract. The decider stays k=20 only if resolving
343|three named base sets fits in its 119,410 rows of headroom (929,166 rows today, F-5). If it does
344|not: a two-stage decider (stage 1 resolves bases and collapses, node class, Poseidon; stage 2
345|is today's pairing decider over stage 1), at one more 70 s proof per final proof.
346|
347|The single-run product (`acceptRun` with a result in ledger state) is `acceptRoot` plus
348|`openClaim` in one transaction, or a thin second template over the same decider.
349|
350|## 7. Q6: migration
351|
352|Carries over: the verifier gadget use, accumulator encoding, collapse and genesis-carry
353|constraints of `ivc.rs`; height range checks; the pairing decider (`run_decider.rs`,
354|`pairing.rs`) and the template mechanism; the Lean `Seg`/`link`/`NodeCert` algebra and the
355|Quint slot model; the rule fragments' logic; the witness stream as producer; the profiling
356|harness and row probes.
357|
358|Replaced: node `SHKIVC06` (by N, R, F); the decider's public values and the `acceptRun`
359|contract (by `acceptRoot`); the leaf's carrier hashing and `prog_d` definition; the
360|one-contract-per-program deployment; `Bounds` as a key input.
361|
362|Milestones, each with working software:
363|
364|- M-A (now, no new design): finish the linear chain on P1-P3 as planned. It stays the first
365|  milestone (`general-purpose.md` Consequences) and produces the measured leaf numbers.
366|- M-B GP-4 core: N with named lifts and R over the current leaf statement plus `input_d`;
367|  decider with `[set_root, n]`; `SherlockClaims` with `acceptRoot`/`openClaim`. Acceptance:
368|  chain, balanced tree and fan-out DAG at depth >= 8 over stand-in leaves; then GP-2 (b).
369|- M-C GP-2 (a) and outcomes: `deps_d` in the leaf, seal-with-dependencies, all outcome kinds,
370|  run input, in-circuit genesis.
371|- M-D GP-3: F, the registry, one adapter class; a Compact circuit proved with a Poseidon
372|  transcript; then the Blake2b adapter.
373|- M-E GP-1 capacity: committed memory in U, in the order program table, frames, arena.
374|  A program larger than the old carriers runs.
375|
376|M-B before M-E because the node design does not depend on the leaf's inside, and M-E is the
377|largest rewrite. M-E's statement (`pre_d`, `post_d` are opaque digests to N) is fixed at M-B, so
378|re-keying U at M-E changes only the U constant in R (R, N and D are re-keyed once then).
379|
380|## 8. Q7: experiments, ranked
381|
382|No heavy job is needed for X1-X3 and X7; they are `cost_model` row probes (minutes, a few GB).
383|
384|| # | Hypothesis | Measurement | Kill criterion | Cost |
385||---|---|---|---|---|
386|| X1 | A two-slot node over three named keys fits k=20 with margin; R and F fit k=20 | `cost_model` rows of N {poly, poly}, R {leaf, leaf}, F {witnessed key + path}; needs the name-selection change in a patched gadget | N or R above 0.95 x 2^20 -> fallback B | 1-2 days of code, minutes to run |
387|| X2 | Committed memory makes the leaf independent of `Bounds` at a per-step cost below today's qualification-config hashing plus 3k rows | count distinct cell reads and writes per rule from the reference machine; rows of one step with Merkle and hash-chain openings | median step above 8k rows of memory work | 2-3 days, no proving |
388|| X3 | The decider resolves three named base sets within k=20 | `cost_model` rows of D over N from X1 | above 2^20 -> two-stage decider, measure its second proof | hours after X1 |
389|| X4 | Fallback B is affordable: three-slot node at k=21 | prove time and RSS at k=21 (needs a 2^21 SRS) | above 48 GB or above 2.5x the k=20 step | one heavy job, about 1 h |
390|| X5 | An adapter for the commonest Compact class fits k=20 | rows of `A_c` for (jubjub + poseidon, k of a real contract circuit), public-input cap 1,024 | above 2^20 | 1-2 days, minutes to run |
391|| X6 | Blake2b transcript in the adapter fits k=20 | rows of the Blake2b chip per block x transcript bytes of a real Compact proof | above 2^20 with one verification | 2 days |
392|| X7 | Compact `transientHash` equals the node's Poseidon | hash one vector both ways | mismatch -> claim tree hashed with the Compact hash in circuit, or `openClaim` as a hand-written key | 1 hour |
393|| X8 | Concurrency: P=3 node-class provers hold f3 <= 1.75 with leaf provers beside them | wall and RSS, mixed load | throughput gain below 1.5x | one heavy job |
394|
395|X1 decides between A and B. X2 decides whether GP-1 capacity is a leaf rewrite or a paging
396|layer under the current carriers. X3 and X5 decide the key count and the decider shape.
397|
398|## 9. Open points I am least sure of
399|
400|- The row estimate for N depends on how the accumulator's public-input encoding grows with
401|  three name sets (63 instance lanes today, `prover.md:10`).
402|- Whether Compact circuits always have one instance column and one phase is inferred from the
403|  stdlib's fixed configuration (`ZS:lib.rs:14-27`), not checked on a compiled contract.
404|- `midnight-aggregation` 0.1.0 exists (https://docs.rs/crate/midnight-aggregation/latest,
405|  "Toolkit for proof aggregation of midnight-proofs"); `tree.md` F5 describes it as a linear IVC
406|  aggregator. I did not read its source. If it already offers witnessed-key slots, F is smaller
407|  work.
408|- The seal-with-dependencies rule fixes the order of dependencies in `deps_root`; a run that
409|  awaits claims dynamically (`/2` profile, `D/design.md` D8) needs `deps_d` built in the state.
